purpose: Source-indexed vowel/register/coda evidence register. Rows document cited examples; they are not an adjudicated gold corpus and must not be used as a universal deterministic grapheme-to-IPA table.

status_vocabulary.SOURCE_ATTESTED_NOT_GOLD: A source explicitly provides the form and/or transcription; not independently adjudicated against recordings or multiple lexical sources.
status_vocabulary.CONFLICTING_SOURCE_ANALYSES: Sources provide non-equivalent examples or transcription analyses; preserve alternatives and do not collapse into one universal rule.
status_vocabulary.NOT_ESTABLISHED: No deterministic IPA or Ukrainian output is justified by the current evidence.

unicode17-ch16.role: Authoritative encoding/orthographic reference with illustrative pronunciations; not an acoustic experiment

chem2020.role: Small Phnom Penh acoustic vowel study; four selected speakers and 61 lexical items, useful for bounded open/closed and vowel inventory observations, not a complete cross-product.

mam2025.role: Peer-reviewed conference proceedings acoustic F0 study comparing five Phnom Penh Khmer speakers' PPK and SK productions; prosody evidence only, not vowel-formant or phonation evidence.

wayland-guion2005.role: Preliminary acoustic investigation of colloquial /r/-loss in two male Phnom Penh speakers; later Kirby (2014) reports effects on f0, VOT/aspiration and vowel quality. The accessible source does not establish the wordlist size, repetition count or a matched control design; do not infer these.

kirby2014.role: Peer-reviewed acoustic and perceptual study of colloquial Phnom Penh /CrV/ realizations. Reports 20 participants, 41 reading items and 15 colloquial variants, with production and two perception experiments; four consistent /r/-retaining speakers excluded from acoustic analysis.

Unicode 17 Table 16-7 gives a different illustrative lexical item/transcription for ក; see KHV-008.

cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A's representative inherent-vowel contrast for second-series គ.
limitations: Do not generalize to every coda, lexical environment, or dialect.
Unicode 17 Table 16-7 gives a different illustrative lexical item/transcription for គ; see KHV-008.

cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A's example of a series-conditioned realization of the same dependent vowel sign.
limitations: One representative form; not a full sign-by-series matrix.

cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A's contrast with កី; demonstrates that the dependent sign does not have one invariant vowel value.
limitations: One representative form; not a full sign-by-series matrix.

cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A's example of dependent vowel ា after a first-series consonant.
limitations: Not sufficient to infer the value in closed syllables or other profiles.

cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A's contrast with កា; illustrates series-conditioned vowel interpretation.
limitations: Not sufficient to infer the value in closed syllables or other profiles.

cases.register_condition: NIKAHIT coda/nucleus context; Unicode 17 lexical illustration
cases.phonological_interpretation: Unicode 17.0 and R12A give materially different source transcriptions for this lexical item. Preserve each source's transcription convention rather than normalizing silently.
limitations: The sources report the same written lexical form with non-equivalent transcriptions.
The difference may involve both onset representation and vowel quality; do not attribute it solely to register or NIKAHIT.
No independent audio-based or multi-source adjudication has been recorded.
Do not generalize to all NIKAHIT spellings.

alternatives.note: Unicode 17.0 Chapter 16 illustrative lexical transcription; encoding/orthographic reference, not acoustic adjudication.
R12A rhyme table transcription; preserve source convention verbatim.

cases.selection_criterion: Do not choose a universal project IPA from these source forms alone. Verify the lexical identity and transcription conventions, then adjudicate dialect and segment values independently.

cases.orthography: ក / គ (Unicode 17 Table 16-7 illustrative lexical examples)
cases.register_condition: Unicode 17 Table 16-7; distinct lexical glosses and bracketed transcriptions
cases.phonological_interpretation: Unicode 17 gives ក ‘neck’ [kɔː] and គ ‘mute’ [kɔ̀ː], which are not interchangeable with R12A's simplified ក /kɑː/ vs គ /kɔː/ examples.

alternatives.forms: ក vs គ representative contrast

cases.selection_criterion: Retain both source-specific examples; do not promote either pair into a universal register-to-vowel mapping until lexical identity, transcription convention, dialect and context are reconciled.
limitations: The sources need not be describing the same lexical items or phonetic context.
A phonological class contrast is supported; a universal deterministic mapping is not.

cases.register_condition: plain coda vs COENG/subscript cluster; syllabification differs
cases.phonological_interpretation: Unicode 17's contrast illustrates that changing the orthographic/syllabic structure changes the vowel outcome; not a generic coda substitution rule.
limitations: The two transcriptions are retained as source-specific contrast examples, not an adjudicated dialect-normalized gold pair.

cases.register_condition: second-series base ព + dependent vowel U+17B6 + written coda ម
cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A uses ពាម as the comparison form for ពាំ to illustrate that NIKAHIT changes the sound value of the vowel sign U+17B6.
cases.source_locator: Khmer Orthography Notes, §Coda diacritics, lines 1250–1258; comparison ពាម / ពាំ.
limitations: The source uses the pair to illustrate a nucleus effect but does not provide a word-level IPA transcription here; IPA remains null.
Do not infer a general vowel value for every NIKAHIT combination.

cases.register_condition: second-series base ព + dependent vowel U+17B6 + NIKAHIT U+17C6
cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A explicitly contrasts ពាំ with ពាម as an example of NIKAHIT changing the sound value of the vowel sign U+17B6.
cases.source_locator: Khmer Orthography Notes, §Coda diacritics, lines 1250–1258; comparison ពាម / ពាំ.
limitations: The source does not provide a word-level IPA transcription for this token in the cited passage; IPA remains null.
NIKAHIT affects both coda and nucleus; do not model it as a generic independent vowel sign.

cases.register_condition: first-series base ខ + dependent vowel U+17B6 + coda ត; no BANTOC
cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A uses ខាត as the long-vowel comparison for ខាត់ when explaining the shortening effect of U+17CB BANTOC.
cases.source_locator: Khmer Orthography Notes, §Vowel modifier marks, lines 332–348; comparison ខាត / ខាត់.
limitations: The source gives a relative length example, not a word-level IPA transcription; IPA remains null.
Do not assign a numeric duration or infer all short/long outcomes from the spelling pair.

cases.register_condition: first-series base ខ + dependent vowel U+17B6 + coda ត + BANTOC U+17CB
cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A states that U+17CB BANTOC basically shortens the preceding vowel and illustrates this with ខាត់ compared with ខាត.
cases.source_locator: Khmer Orthography Notes, §Vowel modifier marks, lines 332–348; comparison ខាត / ខាត់.
limitations: The source gives a relative length example, not a word-level IPA transcription; IPA remains null.
Do not assign a numeric duration or infer all short/long outcomes from the spelling pair.

cases.register_condition: second-series base ជ + U+17D0 vowel modifier + final រ
cases.phonological_interpretation: R12A states that final រ is usually silent, but the combination U+17D0 + U+179A produces the sound ɔə; ជ័រ is the cited example.
cases.source_locator: Khmer Orthography Notes, §§Diphthongs and rhymes / Vowel modifier marks, lines 318–324 and 332–342.
limitations: The source specifies the vowel sequence's sound but does not provide a full word-level IPA transcription here; IPA remains null.
Do not generalize this special U+17D0 + រ sequence to all final រ contexts.

coverage_policy: Rows with ukrainian_adaptation=null are deliberate: the repository has a proposed segment adapter, but these word-level outputs have not been adjudicated and must not be presented as confident lexical transcriptions.

context_dimensions.environment: base consonant class × inherent/dependent vowel sign; register shifters may change class
context_dimensions.finding: R12A explicitly illustrates ក /kɑː/ vs គ /kɔː/, កី /kəj/ vs គី /kiː/, and កា /kaː/ vs គា /kiə/.
context_dimensions.locator: Khmer Orthography Notes, §§Consonant registers and Inherent vowels, lines 235–266; examples table lines 237–243.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: Modern Khmer orthographic pronunciation reference; not a balanced contemporary Phnom Penh acoustic experiment.
context_dimensions.implementation: Use as four source-attested open-syllable examples only. Do not extrapolate to every sign, coda, or profile.

context_dimensions.environment: two-syllable words where the second syllable begins with a sonorant
context_dimensions.finding: The second syllable may take the first syllable's vowel class when its onset is one of ង ញ ណ ន ម យ ឡ ល រ វ; explicit exceptions are noted.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: Descriptive modern Khmer synthesis; no complete contemporary Phnom Penh lexical list or exception inventory.
context_dimensions.implementation: Keep as a lexical/contextual dependency. Never overwrite the second base consonant's underlying orthographic class globally.

context_dimensions.environment: stressed vs unstressed vowels; first syllable of many bisyllabic words
context_dimensions.finding: R12A maps several vowel phones with following glottal closure in stressed syllables but not unstressed; many bisyllabic words have an unstressed first syllable realized as schwa in colloquial speech, while compounds may differ.
context_dimensions.locator: Khmer Orthography Notes, §Phonetic syllables lines 201–209; vowel mapping legend lines 491–496 and entries lines 503–615.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: General modern Khmer description with explicit colloquial qualification; not a controlled Phnom Penh stress experiment.
context_dimensions.implementation: Stress and word structure must be explicit inputs or remain unresolved. Do not inject glottal stops or schwa solely from spelling.

context_dimensions.environment: U+17C6 NIKAHIT, U+17C7 REAHMUK, U+17CB BANTOC, and series-2 U+17D0 before different final places
context_dimensions.finding: NIKAHIT and REAHMUK represent /-m/ and /-h/ and also affect the nucleus; BANTOC shortens the preceding vowel. For ɔ-class forms with U+17D0, the cited rhymes distinguish velar finals (/eə̆/) from non-velar finals (/oə̆/).
context_dimensions.locator: Khmer Orthography Notes, §§Nikahit and reahmuk lines 325–347; vowel mapping entries lines 753–826; coda tables around lines 1240–1265.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: Specialist descriptive mapping; exact contemporary Phnom Penh token distributions and full coda inventory are not acoustically cross-tabulated.
context_dimensions.implementation: Model the coda and nucleus jointly. Do not treat ំ/ះ as independent vowels or reduce every ់ form by a fixed universal duration.

context_dimensions.environment: open vs closed syllable; coda present
context_dimensions.finding: Chem reports closed syllables are usually shorter and that final consonants can modify nucleus quality and length; short diphthongs are reported in closed contexts with /-h, -k, -ʔ/.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: Phnom Penh acoustic sample: 21 speakers screened, four selected speakers (two female), 61 lexical items, three formal-reading repetitions.
context_dimensions.implementation: Use as a coda/syllable-context risk flag, not a complete coda-conditioned IPA rule. The paper reports inconsistent duration units/values and does not supply a full vowel × coda × series table.

context_dimensions.environment: Phnom Penh vs Standard Khmer lexical diphthong contrasts
context_dimensions.finding: Chem reports /tiɜ/ vs /tiət/ as distinct in Standard Khmer but merged in the studied Phnom Penh variety; likewise /eː/ vs /ɛe/ is reported merged as /eː/ in Phnom Penh.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: Four-speaker Phnom Penh sample; article explicitly states Standard Khmer is not a sharply defined variety and notes regional/speaker variation.
context_dimensions.implementation: Keep as profile-specific lexical contrasts. Do not implement a global phoneme merger from two examples.

context_dimensions.environment: underlying obstruent+/r/ onset in careful-reading vs colloquial Phnom Penh speech
context_dimensions.finding: Wayland and Guion's preliminary acoustic study reports differences in post-release aspiration/VOT, f0 and vowel quality between reading and colloquial Phnom Penh /CrV/ forms in two male speakers. The accessible account does not establish the wordlist size, repetition count or matched /CV/ and /ChV/ control design.
context_dimensions.locator: Wayland & Guion 2005, Mon-Khmer Studies 35, pp. 55–82; DOI 10.15144/MKSJ-35.55.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: Two male Phnom Penh speakers. The accessible paper summary and Kirby (2014) citation establish the speaker count and acoustic dimensions, but not a verified wordlist size or repetition count.
context_dimensions.implementation: Treat as preliminary evidence for a colloquial /CrV/ pathway only. Do not generalize to all consonants, vowel classes or careful speech; do not infer missing sample counts or controls.

context_dimensions.environment: Phnom Penh vs Standard Khmer; r>h clusters and voiced-onset disyllables
context_dimensions.finding: Mam et al. report a lower F0 group in PPK for r>h onsets and voiced-onset disyllabic words; five speakers and 50 words were analyzed, with three repetitions and F0 measured on the stressed rime. The authors interpret the categorical separation as possible phonologized high/low pitch.
context_dimensions.locator: Mam, Pittayaporn & Maspong 2025, TAI pp. 138–143; §§2–4, DOI 10.21437/TAI.2025-29.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: Five native speakers aged 20–25 from greater Phnom Penh; PPK and SK elicitation. F0 only; no vowel formants, voice quality, or perception test.
context_dimensions.implementation: Keep pitch as a separate profile/prosody layer. Do not encode a general lexical tone or derive tone marks from graphemes. The stressed disyllabic r>h examples use a single [r] onset; the authors explicitly request more cluster-onset words to test this context, and no perception test is reported.

context_dimensions.environment: coeng chains, unmarked vowel absence, consonant stacking and orthographic syllable boundaries
context_dimensions.finding: Khmer orthographic units do not always coincide with phonetic syllables; coengs can encode onset clusters or syllable chaining, and absence of a vowel may be unmarked. A consonant sequence may have competing syllabifications without lexical context.
context_dimensions.locator: Unicode L2/22-290, §§Orthographic Syllable Structure and Coengs, pp. 9–10; R12A §§Phonetic syllables and Unmarked vowel absence, lines 201–215 and 1095–1115.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: Orthographic/structural evidence, not acoustic resolution of individual ambiguous words.
context_dimensions.implementation: Resolve structure before vowel rules. If lexical segmentation/coda role is ambiguous, keep IPA unresolved rather than guessing.

context_dimensions.environment: Phnom Penh colloquial /CrV/ vs careful/reading /CrV/, /CV/ and /ChV/ forms
context_dimensions.finding: Kirby reports colloquial /CrV/ forms with lower F0, increased VOT/post-release aspiration, spectral-balance changes and diphthongization of low vowels. In perception, F0 is a sufficient cue; aspiration and breathiness can reinforce it, while F1/F2 vowel-height changes are not a reliable lexical cue in the tested continua.
context_dimensions.locator: Kirby 2014, Journal of Phonetics 43, pp. 69–85; production methods/results §§3.1–3.3; perception experiments §§4.1–4.2; synthesis §5. DOI 10.1016/j.wocn.2014.02.001.
context_dimensions.profile_scope: 20 Phnom Penh participants; four who consistently retained /r/ were excluded from acoustic analysis. 41 reading items × 3 repetitions and 15 colloquial variants × 3 repetitions; 2,664 tokens recorded, 2,099 obstruent-onset tokens analyzed. Two perception experiments used synthesized continua.
context_dimensions.implementation: Keep this as a separate colloquial profile. The observed low-vowel movement is context-specific and F1/F2 was not a reliable perceptual lexical cue; do not turn the acoustic diphthongization into a universal vowel rewrite or tonal mark.
